title: Enforcement Decree of the Act on Research, Development and Promotion of Agro-Healing
title_original: 치유농업 연구개발 및 육성에 관한 법률 시행령
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on Research, Development and Promotion of Agro-Healing and matters necessary for its enforcement.

Article 2 (Duties of Agro-Healing Specialists)
(1) "Specialized duties prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as the development and implementation of agro-healing programs" in subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Act on Research, Development and Promotion of Agro-Healing (hereinafter referred to as the "Act") means the following duties:
1. Development and implementation of agro-healing programs;
2. Planning and business management of agro-healing services;
3. Operation and management of agro-healing services;
4. Education and management of personnel in the field of agro-healing;
5. Operation and management of agro-healing resources and agro-healing facilities.
(2) Agro-healing specialists shall be classified into Grade I agro-healing specialists and Grade II agro-healing specialists and shall perform the duties in the following categories:
1. Grade I agro-healing specialists: The duties prescribed in paragraph (1) 1 through 5;
2. Grade II agro-healing specialists: The duties prescribed in paragraph (1) 1, 3, and 5.

Article 3 (Formulation of Comprehensive Plans and Implementation Plans, Etc.)
(1) Where the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration intends to formulate or amend a comprehensive plan for research, development and promotion of agro-healing under the former part of Article 5 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as a "comprehensive plan"), the Administrator shall undergo deliberation by the Rural Development Project Deliberative Committee under Article 6 of the Rural Development Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Rural Development Project Deliberative Committee").
(2) Where the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration intends to formulate a comprehensive plan, the Administrator shall, after undergoing deliberation by the Rural Development Project Deliberative Committee pursuant to paragraph (1), undergo deliberation by the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology under the Presidential Advisory Council on Science and Technology Act pursuant to the latter part of Article 5 (1) of the Act.
(3) Where the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration intends to formulate or amend an annual implementation plan under Article 5 (3) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan"), the Administrator shall undergo deliberation by the Rural Development Project Deliberative Committee.
(4) An implementation plan shall include the following matters:
1. Performance and evaluation of the preceding year's implementation plan;
2. The direction and goals for research, development and promotion of agro-healing for the relevant year;
3. Detailed implementation plans and investment plans for each project;
4. Other matters that the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration recognizes as necessary for research, development and promotion of agro-healing.
(5) Where the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration formulates or amends a comprehensive plan or implementation plan, the Administrator shall publicly notify its contents in the Official Gazette or post them on the website of the Rural Development Administration, etc.

Article 4 (Changes to Minor Matters) "Where minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree have been changed" in the proviso to Article 5 (5) of the Act means the following cases:
1. Where a project period prescribed in a comprehensive plan or implementation plan has been shortened or extended by up to two years;
2. Where the method of implementing a project has been changed without changing the contents of the project in a comprehensive plan or implementation plan;
3. Where changes resulting from the enactment, amendment, or repeal of other statutes have been reflected;
4. Where a simple mistake, clerical error, omission, or equivalent obvious error has been corrected.

Article 5 (Research, Development, Dissemination, Etc.)
(1) Where necessary to efficiently carry out research, development, dissemination, etc. under the subparagraphs of Article 8 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "research, development, etc."), the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration may commission research services from a research institution or organization in the field of agro-healing or seek advice from experts, etc. in the field of agro-healing.
(2) The specific contents of dissemination and pilot projects for the field application of agro-healing services under Article 8 (1) 4 of the Act shall be as follows:
1. Projects to support commercialization of technologies related to agro-healing services;
2. Projects to establish and improve agro-healing facilities;
3. Projects for cooperation with institutions, organizations, and specialized personnel related to agro-healing services;
4. Other projects that the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration recognizes as necessary for the field application of agro-healing services.
(3) In addition to matters prescribed in paragraphs (1) and (2), specific methods of carrying out research, development, etc. shall be determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration.

Article 6 (Eligibility to Take the Qualifying Examination for Agro-Healing Specialists, etc.)
(1) The qualifying examination for agro-healing specialists under Article 11 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the “qualifying examination”) shall be administered separately for Grade I agro-healing specialists and Grade II agro-healing specialists; eligibility to take the examination, examination subjects, and passing criteria for each qualification grade of agro-healing specialist shall be as specified in attached Table 1.
(2) The qualifying examination shall be divided into the following parts: <Amended on June 20, 2024>
1. First stage of the qualifying examination: A multiple-choice examination;
2. Second stage of the qualifying examination: A written examination combining essay questions and short-answer questions.
(3) The second stage of the qualifying examination shall be limited to persons who have passed the first stage of the qualifying examination and persons exempted from the first stage of the qualifying examination.
(4) A person who has passed the first stage of the qualifying examination shall be exempted from the first stage of the qualifying examination only at the next examination session. <Amended on June 20, 2024>
(5) Where the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration intends to administer the qualifying examination, the Administrator shall publicly announce the date and time of the examination, the examination venue, the period for submitting examination applications, and other matters necessary for the examination on the website of the Rural Development Administration (where duties concerning the administration and management of the qualifying examination have been entrusted pursuant to Article 11 (2), meaning the website of the institution entrusted with those duties), etc., no later than 60 days before the examination date.
(6) A person who intends to take the qualifying examination shall submit an examination application prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
(7) A person who intends to take the qualifying examination shall pay, in revenue stamps, an examination fee determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration in consideration of the costs necessary to administer the qualifying examination for agro-healing specialists. Provided, That where the application is submitted over the Internet, the fee shall be paid by electronic money, electronic payment, or the like through an information and communications network. <Added on June 20, 2024>
(8) Matters necessary for the administration and management of the qualifying examination, other than those prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (7), shall be determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration. <Amended on June 20, 2024>

Article 7 (Assignment of Agro-Healing Specialists)
(1) Pursuant to Article 11 (7) of the Act, the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration shall assign at least one Grade I or Grade II agro-healing specialist to a department of an affiliated institution that is dedicated to providing agro-healing services or education related to agro-healing.
(2) Pursuant to Article 11 (7) of the Act, the head of a local government shall assign at least one Grade I or Grade II agro-healing specialist to a department dedicated to providing agro-healing services or education related to agro-healing in an affiliated local rural development institution (meaning a local rural development institution under Article 3 of the Rural Development Act).

Article 8 (Revocation of Qualifications of Agro-Healing Specialists, etc.)
Detailed criteria for revocation or suspension of the qualification of an agro-healing specialist under Article 12 (1) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 2.

Article 9 (Requirements for Designation of Agro-Healing Specialist Training Institutions)
The requirements for designation of an agro-healing specialist training institution under Article 13 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as an “agro-healing specialist training institution”) shall be as specified in attached Table 3.

Article 10 (Revocation of Designation of Agro-Healing Specialist Training Institutions, etc.)
“Where matters prescribed by Presidential Decree have been violated” in Article 14 (1) 3 of the Act means the following cases:
1. Where an agro-healing specialist training course has not been opened within one year from the date of designation as an agro-healing specialist training institution pursuant to Article 13 (1) of the Act;
2. Where the agro-healing specialist training institution has not operated for a continuous period of one year or longer without justifiable grounds.

Article 10-2 (Certification Standards for Excellent Agro-Healing Facilities, etc.)
(1) The certification standards for excellent agro-healing facilities under Article 15 (1) and (3) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 3-2.
(2) The Administrator of the Rural Development Administration may annually verify whether an excellent agro-healing facility certified pursuant to Article 15 (3) of the Act meets the certification standards under attached Table 3-2.
(3) Details necessary for the certification standards and verification of excellent agro-healing facilities under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be determined and publicly notified by the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration.

Article 11 (Delegation and Entrustment of Authority, etc.)
(1) Pursuant to Article 18 (1) of the Act, the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration shall delegate the authority to conduct safety and hygiene education under Article 8 (3) of the Act to Special Metropolitan City Mayors, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, Do Governors, and Special Self-Governing Province Governors. <Amended on June 20, 2024>
(2) Pursuant to Article 18 (2) of the Act, the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration shall entrust the following duties to the Korea Agriculture Technology Promotion Agency under Article 33 of the Rural Development Act: <Amended on February 22, 2022; June 20, 2024>
1. Supporting the commercialization of technologies related to agro-healing and business start-ups under Article 9 of the Act;
2. Conducting and administering qualifying examinations under Article 11 (1) of the Act;
3. Duties concerning certification of excellent agro-healing facilities, renewal of the validity period, and collection of fees under Article 15 of the Act (including duties concerning checks on excellent agro-healing facilities under Article 10-2 (2)).

Article 12 (Processing of Personally Identifiable Information)
The Administrator of the Rural Development Administration (including persons entrusted with the duties of the Administrator of the Rural Development Administration pursuant to Article 11 (2)) may process data containing resident registration numbers under subparagraph 1 of Article 19 of the Enforcement Decree of the Personal Information Protection Act where unavoidable for performing the following affairs:
1. Affairs concerning the conduct and administration of qualifying examinations under Article 11 (1) of the Act;
2. Affairs concerning verification of grounds for disqualification of agro-healing specialists and issuance of agro-healing specialist qualification certificates, etc. under Article 11 (3) and (6) of the Act;
3. Affairs concerning revocation and suspension of the qualifications of agro-healing specialists under Article 12 of the Act.

Article 12-2 (Review of Regulations)
The Administrator of the Rural Development Administration shall review the appropriateness of the criteria for certification of excellent agro-healing facilities under Article 10-2 and attached Table 3-2 every three years, counting from January 1, 2024 (meaning before the date corresponding to the base date in every third year), and take measures such as making improvements.

Article 13 (Criteria for Imposition of Administrative Fines)
The criteria for imposition of administrative fines under Article 20 (1) and (2) of the Act shall be as specified in attached Table 4. <Amended on June 20, 2024>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 31545, March 23, 2021>

This Decree shall enter into force on March 25, 2021.

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Rural Development Act) <Presidential Decree No. 32503, February 22, 2022>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on March 1, 2022.

Article 2 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (7) Omitted.
(8) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Research, Development and Promotion of Agro-Healing is partially amended as follows:
In the part other than the subparagraphs of Article 11 (2), "Foundation of Agricultural Technology Commercialization and Transfer" shall be replaced by "Korea Agriculture Technology Promotion Agency".

ADDENDA (Enforcement Decree of the Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Systems) <Presidential Decree No. 33004, November 29, 2022>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on December 1, 2022. <Proviso omitted.>

Articles 2 through 15 Omitted.

Article 16 (Amendment of Other Statutes)
(1) through (33) Omitted.
(34) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on Research, Development and Promotion of Agro-Healing is partially amended as follows:
In subparagraph 1 (d) of attached Table 3, "Act on Fire Prevention and Installation, Maintenance, and Safety Control of Firefighting Systems" shall be replaced by "Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Systems", and "Article 9 (1)" shall be replaced by "Article 12 (1)".
(35) through (39) Omitted.

Article 17 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 34587, June 20, 2024>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on June 21, 2024: Provided, That the amended provisions of Article 6 (7) shall enter into force on January 1, 2025.

Article 2 (Applicability to Qualifying Examinations for Agro-Healing Specialists)
The amended provisions of Article 6 (2) 2 shall begin to apply to qualifying examinations for agro-healing specialists publicly announced after this Decree enters into force.

Article 3 (Transitional Measures concerning Exemption from the First Stage of Qualifying Examinations for Agro-Healing Specialists)
The former provisions shall apply to persons who passed the first stage of the qualifying examination for agro-healing specialists before this Decree enters into force, notwithstanding the amended provisions of Article 6 (4).

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 36434, June 23, 2026>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Applicability to Eligibility to Take Qualifying Examinations for Grade I Agro-Healing Specialists)
The amended provisions of subparagraph 1 (a) 1) of attached Table 1 shall begin to apply to qualifying examinations publicly announced after this Decree enters into force.
